methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Amca, a robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jai Malik and Eli Giovanetti, is preparing for IPO after raising $76.5M in total capital. The relevant peer universe consists of 10 companies operating in Robotics & Manufacturing, comprising 1 publicly traded entity (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. While 10 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the filtering criteria for stage-aligned or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient sample size. Specifically, zero same-stage IPO-ready robotics companies, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier entities emerged from the dataset, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the heterogeneity of business models, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines across the broader Robotics & Manufacturing segment.

Without sufficient narrow peer triangulation, this valuation analysis cannot be completed using the available data. A defensible range would require either: expansion of the comparable set beyond stage and tier constraints with explicit discount/premium adjustments, detailed financial metrics from the identified private peers (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics), or alternative methods such as DCF or precedent transaction analysis. The IPO timing creates urgency, but proceeding with incomplete comparables would compromise analytical rigor.
